title: JTAG TAP (Test Access Port)
summary: JTAG (IEEE 1149.1) provides a serial interface for testing and debugging. TAP controller: 16-state FSM controlled by TMS (Test Mode Select) and TCK (Test Clock). Registers: IR (Instruction Register), DR (Data Register, includes IDCODE, BYPASS, BOUNDARY SCAN). Operations: shift instructions into IR, then shift data through DR. Used for boundary scan testing, flash programming, and CPU debugging.

structure.meaning: Controls the TAP state machine. Sampled on rising TCK edge.
Serial data input. Shifted into IR or DR.
Serial data output. Shifted out of IR or DR.
Holds the current instruction. Common: IDCODE (read device ID), BYPASS (1-bit pass-through), SAMPLE/PRELOAD (boundary scan), EXTEST (external test).
Data register selected by IR. IDCODE (32 bits: version (4) + part number (16) + manufacturer (11) + 1), BYPASS (1 bit), BOUNDARY SCAN (chain of boundary scan cells).
Test-Logic-Reset, Run-Test/Idle, Select-DR-Scan, Capture-DR, Shift-DR, Exit1-DR, Pause-DR, Exit2-DR, Update-DR, Select-IR-Scan, Capture-IR, Shift-IR, Exit1-IR, Pause-IR, Exit2-IR, Update-IR.

notes: JTAG is used for hardware debugging, flash programming, and boundary scan testing.
JTAG is the primary interface for debugging embedded systems and SoCs.
Boundary scan tests PCB connections by shifting test patterns through boundary scan cells.
JTAG can be used to program flash memory (e.g., SPI flash via JTAG).
SWD (Serial Wire Debug) is ARM's 2-wire alternative to JTAG.
